note: Single Language URL Prefix keeps the language URL prefix (e.g. /en) on a site with only one enabled language, which core normally drops. It works via a path processor (single_language_url_prefix.path_processor / SingleLanguageNegotiationUrl) and only acts when exactly one language is enabled and core language negotiation URL source is path prefix with a prefix set. Its own persistent state is a single config value single_language_url_prefix.settings.excluded_paths (newline-separated paths/patterns, matched with core path.matcher) listing paths that keep working WITHOUT the prefix; the settings form is /admin/config/regional/language/single-language-url-prefix (permission administer languages). The module ships default config but no config schema, so excluded_paths is an untyped string. Medium cases read the live excluded_paths value; hard cases set excluded_paths, verified live. Baselines are restored explicitly (excluded_paths => '') since State is unreliable on this site.

evals.prompt: What problem does the Drupal single_language_url_prefix module solve, and when would I need it?
evals.expected_output: Core only adds the language URL prefix (e.g. /en) when more than one language is enabled; on a single-language (monolingual) site it drops the prefix. This module re-adds the prefix for the single-language case via a path processor, so URLs keep their language segment.

evals.prompt: Using single_language_url_prefix, how do I stop certain paths (like /admin) from getting the language prefix, and where is that list stored?
evals.expected_output: Add them to the Excluded Paths list on the settings form at /admin/config/regional/language/single-language-url-prefix (one path per line, wildcards allowed, matched with core's path.matcher). It is stored in single_language_url_prefix.settings.excluded_paths.

evals.prompt: For single_language_url_prefix to actually add the prefix to URLs, how must Drupal's core language negotiation be configured?
evals.expected_output: Core URL language negotiation must be enabled with source = path prefix and a prefix configured for the single language (language.negotiation url: source path_prefix, prefixes: {<langcode>: '<prefix>'}). It also only acts when exactly one language is enabled; with two or more the module is a no-op.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, single_language_url_prefix has some paths configured to be excluded from the language prefix. Inspect the live configuration and list the excluded path(s).
On this Drupal site, which path pattern is currently excluded from the single_language_url_prefix language prefix? Inspect the live configuration and state the pattern.

On this Drupal site, configure single_language_url_prefix so that the admin area is excluded from the language URL prefix: exclude both the path /admin and the pattern /admin/*. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set single_language_url_prefix.settings.excluded_paths to include a line '/admin' and a line '/admin/*' (via the Excluded Paths textarea on /admin/config/regional/language/single-language-url-prefix, or by saving the config).

evals.prompt: My one-language site adds a /en to the front of every URL, but my API endpoints under /api/ are called by other systems and must not get that language bit. Please make everything under /api/ skip the language prefix, and save it on the live site.
evals.expected_output: Add the pattern /api/* to single_language_url_prefix.settings.excluded_paths (via the Excluded Paths textarea on the module's settings form, or by saving the config) so paths under /api are served without the language prefix.
